summary: Baileys fork aliases libsignal to third-party scope at mutable @latest
details: zero2-baileys@3.6.0 declares its `libsignal` dependency as `npm:@otaxayun/libsignal-node@latest` in package.json. The alias points at an unrelated third-party npm scope with no version pin and no integrity check, so each `npm install` resolves `@latest` fresh and installs whatever that scope currently publishes. The resolved package is then loaded via `require("libsignal")` in lib/Signal/libsignal.js, which routes all end-to-end encrypt/decrypt operations through it, placing attacker-controlled code inside the Signal/crypto path of any bot built on this fork. The dependency source is off-registry in effect (an unrelated-scope alias at a mutable tag) and whoever controls `@otaxayun/libsignal-node` can ship arbitrary code into every installer on any subsequent install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
